 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 14.1.2019.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2(a) That on 14.1.2019 at about 2.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding his Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-03-JK-2506 from Veeranna Palya towards his office at Manyatha Tech Park slowly and cautiously, when he reached near Muneshwara Temple, Verannapalya, outer ring road, service road, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of the KTM Duke motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-HZ-2746 (hereinafter this vehicle has been referred to as offending vehicle) was riding the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

2(b) It is further pleaded that immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 8 days from 14.1.2019 to 21.1.2019.
He was discharged with an advise of follow-up treatment.
The petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards medicine and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.

2(c) It is further case of the petitioner that at the time of the accident the petitioner was aged about 43 years and he was working as a Marketing Executive and getting an income of Rs.1,000/- per day.
On account of accidental injuries the petitioner did not attend his work.
The disability arising out of the accidental injuries would not permit him to do work as he was doing prior to the accident.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
3. In response to the notice the respondents No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective advocates on record and filed the written statement.
4(a) The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner as false.
The respondent No.1 has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained, avocation, age and income of the petitioner as false.
However, it is admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 and it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: It is the defense of the respondent No.1 that the accident was occurred at the middle of the road and it was a head-on-collision.
As the petitioner was in hurry to reach his office, he rode his motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the offending vehicle.
If the petitioner took little care, the accident could have been avoided.
4(c) It is another defense of the respondent No.1 that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
It is contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5(a) The respondent No.2 in his written statement has contended that the alleged accident was occurred at the middle of the road and it was a head on collision.
If the petitioner took little bit care the accident could have been avoided.
Hence, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
5(b) It is further contended that respondent No.2 has taken a policy from the respondent No.1 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
The rider of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective license at the time of accident.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of these pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 14.1.2019 at about 2.45 p.m. near Muneshwara Temple, Veeranna palya outer ring road, service road, Bengaluru 45 due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the KTM Duke motor cycle bearing registration No.KA01-HZ-2746 in actionable negligence?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

from whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. The petitioner to prove his case he himself examined as PW1 and also examined Medical Record Officer of Manipal Hospital, namely Subramanya T.K. as examined as PW2 and Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW3 and got the documents marked at Ex.P1 to P20.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined Billing Manager, Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as RW1 and got the documents marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
8.

3  REASONS Issue No.1:
9.

It is the case of the petitioner that this accident is due to rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending vehicle, whereas the respondent No.1 and 2 have denied the entire case of the petitioner as false, and have taken up the defense that this accident is due to fault of the petitioner but there is no negligence or rashness on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
10. PW1 in his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P7
. Ex .
P1 is the true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.7/2019 of Chickajala Traffic Police Station.
Ex . P2
is the true copy of the first information statement given by the petitioner.
Ex . P3
is the true copy of the spot mahazer.
Ex.P4 is the true copy of IMV report.
Ex.P5 is the true copy of the wound certificate of the petitioner.
Ex.P6 is the true copy of the sketch.
Ex.P7 is the true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.07/2019 of Chickajala Traffic Police Station.

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner himself while he was in the hospital, the H.C. 76 of Chickajala Police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the respondent No.2 alleging that he has committed the offense punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
11.
The respondents to prove their defense that this accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle has not examined any witnesses.

Though the respondent No.2 who is the rider cum owner of the offending vehicle appeared and filed written statement denying the case of the petitioner did not step into the witness box to prove his defence and to disprove the case of the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.1 ought to have been examined the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to disprove the case of the petitioner.

For the best reason known to the respondent No.1 the respondent No.1 neither examined the rider of the offending vehicle nor any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and false case was registered to claim compensation.
13.

Though PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

From the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to P7, it is no doubt that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: The petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- under different heads.

15. In Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another case, which is reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down general principles relating to compensation in injury cases and the heads under which compensation to be awarded in personal injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By keeping the principle laid down in the above cited decision let this court to award the compensation under different heads:
i. LOSS OF EARNINGS:
(a) Loss of future earning on account of permanent disability:
16.

In the Raj Kumar's case referred supra the Hon'ble Supreme Court has also held that "Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss that is percentage of loss of earning capacity arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability."

Further,
at para No.10 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has elaborately discussed with examples and also given three steps for ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

By keeping the guidelines and three steps required to be followed, let this tribunal to assess the functional disability of the petitioner.
17.
The petitioner in his petition as well as in his evidence has stated that due to grievous injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered permanent disability.
In view of the same he is unable to attend his work.

18. The petitioner to prove the disability sustained by him in the alleged accident has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.3.
P.W.3 in his examination- in-chief has deposed that he has been working as an orthopedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: The petitioner came to their hospital with a history of road traffic accident occurred on 14.1.2019.
PW3 further deposed that on examination he found the open fracture of the right tibia upper third leg and type II fracture of the lower third of the right tibia with fracture of the right fibula.
19. PW3 further deposed that petitioner was treated in Columbia Asia hospital till 22.1.2019.
During that period petitioner was underwent wound debridement and CRIF with CC screws on 15.1.2019 slab application, thereafter petitioner was discharged with the advice of follow-up treatment.
PW3 further deposed that petitioner has taken follow-up treatment and the fractures are united.
He has further deposed that on 25.8.2020 implants were removed.
20. PW3 further deposed that as per the clinical test petitioner has 48% physical disability of right lower limb and whole body disability is 16%.
21. PW3 was subjected to cross-examination on behalf of the respondent No.1.
PW3 in his cross- examination has deposed that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has further deposed that he has Ramnaiah.

5 not seen the treatment records of the petitioner.
PW3 has further deposed that fractures of bones reunited.
PW3 further deposed that he is not aware of the profession of the petitioner.
PW3 has denied the suggestion put to him that he has given disability on higher side to help the petitioner and petitioner has no such disability as stated by him in his affidavit.

22. On perusal of the disability assessed in the clinical note at Ex.P19 coupled with oral evidence of PW3 it could be seen that doctor who treated the petitioner has opined that petitioner has permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb to an extent of 48%.
23. The petitioner in his petition has stated that at the time of the accident he was aged about 43 years.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his age.
However unmarked copy of the Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 1.5.1975.
The accident took place on 14.1.2019.
From this document it can be said the petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of accident.
24. The petitioner has stated that prior to the accident he was working as a Marketing Executive and getting Rs.1,000/- per day-.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in respect of his avocation as well as alleged income.
The petitioner in his cross- examination has deposed that he studied up to SSLC.
He has admitted that in the first information statement he has stated that he was working in ANSRGC Company.
He has deposed that his salary was credited to HDFC bank account.
He has further deposed that about 2 years back he has given resignation to his job.

25. Having seen the Ex.P2, first information statement which was lodged by the petitioner himself,
wherein it is stated that he was working in ANSRGC Corporation Pvt. Ltd., at Manyatha Tech Park.
But, the petitioner has not produced any documents with regard to his avocation as well as his income.

If really the petitioner has given resignation and he was not working and he is unable to work due to his injuries sustained in the accident he could have been placed the resignation letter which was also accepted by the company where he was working.

In view of the non- production of the materials, which were in custody of the petitioner with regard to his avocation and income as well as resignation letter it could be inferred that since the petitioner has continued his job he has not produced documents and the same were withheld by him.

26. In the opinion of this Tribunal the injuries sustained and the disability caused to the petitioner would not completely prevent the petitioner from working as an executive or as a supervisor in a company.
But, it may affect for his promotion since he could not able to do the field work efficiently as he was doing earlier.
It is no doubt, the disability caused to the petitioner may affect for carrying out manual work also.

Under the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the view that permanent total disability of 48% of his right lower limb of the petitioner would affect on the avocation of the petitioner to an extent of 12% only not more than that.
27. By considering the income of petitioner of Rs.14,000/- per month, his income per year comes to Rs.1,68,000/-.
Due to 12% disability, annual loss of income would be Rs.20,160/-.
Since the petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of accident, the suitable multiplier is '14'.
So, the loss of future earning capacity due to the said disability of the petitioner is of Rs.2,82,240/-.

Hence, the Ramnaiah.Y vs New India Assurance Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27558058/
6 petitioner is entitled to Rs.2,82,240/- under the head future loss of income.

sentences.text:
(b) Loss of income during laid up period:
28.
The medical documents speak that the petitioner had sustained fractures and he was in the hospital as inpatient for 8 days.

From the case sheet of the petitioner coupled with oral evidence of PW3 it could be seen that the petitioner has taken continues treatment in the hospital as an inpatient from the date of accident dated 14.1.2019 till 21.1.2019.
By considering all these aspects it can be said that the petitioner might have been prevented from earning any income and attending his work for the period of 4 months.

Hence, it is proper to award sum of Rs.56,000/- (14,000/- x 4)
under the head loss of income during the period of taking treatment.

ii. Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines shortly referred to as Medical expenses:
29.

The petitioner in his petition has stated that he has incurred medical expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
as on the date of petition.
The petitioner to prove his medical expenses has produced 21 medicine bills which are collectively marked at Ex.P13.

As per this bills the petitioner has incurred a sum of Rs.14,624/-.
30.
The respondent No.1 in order to prove that entire medical expenses covered under the medical insurance has examined Mr.Santhosh Kumar G.A. billing manager of Manipal Hospital.

RW1 has deposed that sum of Rs.4,07,877/- was covered under the insurance and the petitioner has paid Rs.27,139/-
towards his medical expenses.
RW1 has produced Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
Ex . R1
is the authorisation letter of RW1.
Ex.R2 is the inpatient bill and deposit receipts.
Ex.R3 is the mail of med-assistance insurance Ex.R4 is the copy of the medical insurance policy.

31. Having seen the medical bills produced by the petitioner and RW1 there is no doubt that the Columbia Asia Hospital now it is merged with Manipal Hospital has charged sum of Rs.4,11,295/-
out of which Rs.27,139/- was paid by petitioner and remaining amount was covered under medical insurance.

From this it could be said that though sum of Rs.4,11,295/- was charged towards treatment of the petitioner, petitioner has paid sum of Rs.27,139/- only and remaining amount was covered under the medical insurance.
Hence, it is held that the petitioner is entitled to sum of Rs.27,139/- under the head medical expenses.

iii. Nourishing food expenses, attendant and conveyance:
32.
The proper reunion of the fracture and to gain strength, taking nourishment food is equally necessary along with medicines.
The petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for the period of 8 days.
During that period, one attendant was required for him.
The medical documents and oral evidence of the PW1 speak that the petitioner has visited to Hospital for follow-up treatment.
Therefore, the petitioner has certainly spent expenses for conveyance.

Therefore, sum of Ramnaiah.Y vs New India Assurance Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27558058/
7 Rs.15,000/- is awarded collectively under the heads nourishing food, attendant charges and conveyance.

sentences.text:
iv. Pain, Sufferings and Trauma:
33.
The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient 8 days.

By considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also number of days treatment taken by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that it is just and proper to award the sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner under the head pain and sufferings.

v. Loss of Amenities, discomfort and future happiness:
34.
As noted above, the petitioner has sustained fracture in the accident as a result he has permanent partial disability.
Due to the accidental injuries the petitioner has 48% of permanent disability in his right lower limb.
The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of the accident.
The said disability certainly affects not only on his avocation, but also affects on his amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy his life as he was enjoying earlier prior to the accident.

By overall considering these aspects this Tribunal is of the view that it is just and proper to award Rs.50,000/-
to the petitioner under the head loss of amenities.

vi. Future Medical Expenses:
35.
The petitioner has also claimed future medical expenses.
PW3 in his evidence has stated that the petitioner does not require any future medical treatment.
PW3 has also deposed that implants was also removed.
From this it is clear that the petitioner does not require any future treatment.

Thus,
the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under the head future medical expenses.

Heads of compensation Rs.
Loss of future income on account Rs,2,82,240-00 of permanent disability Loss of income during laid up Rs. 56,000-00 period

Medical Expenses Rs. 27,139-00 Nourishment food expenses, Rs.
15,000-00 attendant & conveyance Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000-00 Loss of amenities Rs.
50,000-00 Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.4,80,379/- rounded up to Rs.4,80,500/- (Rupees Four Lakh Eighty Thousand Five Hundred only).
36. Regarding the liability: While answering issue No.1, it is held that the accident has occurred on account of the rash and negligent riding of rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has admitted that the offending vehicle was covered with valid policy as on the day of the accident.
The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1 has not proved that the respondent No.2 has breached any of the conditions of the policy.
Hence, the respondent No.1-company being an indemnifier of the offending vehicle is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to Ramnaiah.

37. So far as interest on compensation is concerned; this tribunal likes to place reliance upon the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A. 13390/2014 clubbed with M.F.A.
25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018, between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. the Divisional Manager,
the Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has elaborately discussed with regard to the rate of interest to be awarded in the case arising out of the accident, wherein at para No.15 it is held that "However, the provisions of Section 149 (1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in Section 169 of the M.V. Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of C.P.C. to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law over rides the general law.

entities.text:
Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. the Divisional Manager,
the Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of C.P.C.,
1908.
Thus, in the given circumstances of this case, interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

By relying upon the decisions of the aforesaid judgment, this tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
Hence, issue No.2 is answered Accordingly.

Issue No.3:
38.

In view of findings on issue No.1 and 2, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,80,500/- (Rupees Four Lakh Eighty Thousand Five Hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount with up to date interest.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation and the same shall be deposited within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the amount awarded to the petitioner together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any of the Nationalized/Schedule bank of his choice for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through e-payment.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the respondent No.2 alleging that he has committed the offense punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
11.
12. The respondent No.1 ought to have been examined the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to disprove the case of the petitioner.
For the best reason known to the respondent No.1 the respondent No.1 neither examined the rider of the offending vehicle nor any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and false case was registered to claim compensation.
13.
Though PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
From the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to P7, it is no doubt that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
By keeping the guidelines and three steps required to be followed, let this tribunal to assess the functional disability of the petitioner.
17.
In view of the non- production of the materials, which were in custody of the petitioner with regard to his avocation and income as well as resignation letter it could be inferred that since the petitioner has continued his job he has not produced documents and the same were withheld by him.
26. In the opinion of this Tribunal the injuries sustained and the disability caused to the petitioner would not completely prevent the petitioner from working as an executive or as a supervisor in a company.
But, it may affect for his promotion since he could not able to do the field work efficiently as he was doing earlier.
It is no doubt, the disability caused to the petitioner may affect for carrying out manual work also.
Under the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the view that permanent total disability of 48% of his right lower limb of the petitioner would affect on the avocation of the petitioner to an extent of 12% only not more than that.
27. By considering the income of petitioner of Rs.14,000/- per month, his income per year comes to Rs.1,68,000/-.
Due to 12% disability, annual loss of income would be Rs.20,160/-.
Since the petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of accident, the suitable multiplier is '14'.
The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of the accident.
Thus,
the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under the head future medical expenses.

The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,

Draw award accordingly.
